_meta.probe: P1 — temporal retrieval + write-time conflict detection

as_of_retrieval.cause: as_of only reaches graph traversal (_search_graph). The semantic and FTS rankers ignore it entirely, so a past-tense query returns the present.
as_of_retrieval.note: The one apparent pass is not evidence — it is the case where the current-tense control ALSO missed, so the old fact won by accident.

conflict_detection.verdict: FAIL — there is no conflict outcome at all
conflict_detection.worse: One case returned status 'duplicate', meaning the REPLACEMENT FACT WAS SILENTLY REJECTED AND LOST. store() has two outcomes, duplicate and stored; an update that resembles what it replaces takes the first one.

false_positive_sweep.rule: cosine >= threshold AND same memory_type AND >= 1 shared tag
false_positive_sweep.verdict: A usable operating point exists, but only for an ADVISORY signal. At 0.90 the rule fires on essentially nothing (same saturation as consolidation at 0.92). At 0.80 it is ~2 flags per 100 memories — roughly 24 prompts a month at the current ~1200/month write rate, which is tolerable when the action is 'surface this' and not 'merge these'. At 0.70 it is ~100/month, too noisy.
false_positive_sweep.honest_limit: This bounds NOISE, not precision. The corpus has no labelled conflicts, so 2 flags per 100 could be 2 real conflicts or 2 false alarms. The measurement says a detector would not drown the user; it does not say it would find anything.

adoption_decision.bi_temporal_as_of: BUILD. The columns exist unused and the ranker ignores them; this is wiring. 33% accuracy is the baseline to beat.
adoption_decision.conflict_detection: BUILD, advisory only, threshold ~0.80. Never auto-merge on it.
adoption_decision.blocking_bug_first: Fix the silent-rejection bug before either — an update path is pointless while updates are being discarded as duplicates.
